subject.title: fix(telegram): show progress for queued replies

question: Should the shared queued-followup runner permanently expose an optional post-settlement presentation callback for channel-owned cleanup, with Telegram as its first consumer?
rationale: The implementation is narrowly scoped and has proof, but this creates a reusable lifecycle contract whose ordering constrains future channel integrations; that API-shape decision needs the owner of the canonical queued runner.

options.title: Accept the lifecycle seam
options.body: Approve the optional admission/settlement callbacks after the exact-head type checks pass, keeping presentation state owned by the Telegram extension.

options.title: Keep cleanup Telegram-local
options.body: Require a different extension-local seam if maintainers do not want shared follow-up options to expose presentation settlement.

recommendation.title: Accept the lifecycle seam
recommendation.body: Approve the optional admission/settlement callbacks after the exact-head type checks pass, keeping presentation state owned by the Telegram extension.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged queued-followup convergence PR is the closest history for the canonical runner and its lifecycle boundary.
